I can see from the AWS data that there have been successful charging sessions in all of the outlets.
But costumer have got complaints that the DC4 (dispenser right side) does not start charging. Costumer went on site and we tested it and could not get the charging started. That is the test I the timestamps.
Unfortunately the location was busy and there were other charging sessions starting/ongoing at the same time which can make reading the logs much more difficult.
If you look at the logs for the DC4 at the time stamps given can you see why did the test car did not start charging. The costumer stated that that car usually start in Siemens chargers in a first try.

additional_info.subject: 0376368 - ID0376368 - DC/Si-D/FI [MP / P7 170000677] - DC4 does not work CRM:00641000641
additional_info.body:
Hi Sakari, good morning! I hope you are doing well and had a nice weekend.
I am here to save the day!
From the logs that you left here in the description, I also took a look at the logs and found that there seems to be some sort of problem establishin SLAC communication, please take a look:
All the sessions between 12:00:00 and 16:00:00 there was 1 session that worked correctly and charged from ~25mins.
Also I used AWS to check how many sessions were performed correctly since last week.
I see that there were 20 successful charging sessions on this DC4 that you reported that was not working.
I also found that 10 sessions were unsuccessful if we search for when the PilotState changes from B2 to A.
I can think of 3 possibilities here:
CCS cable CP or PP signal is not stable.
We can see that the PilotState changes from A to B2, so I assume if there is any problem it should be the PP.
You need to find around 3V in the PP when the car is connected.
Me and Markus already performed this task once and found that there were 0V in the PP when car is connected. This is after we replaced a cable.
CCS contacts are damaged and only by inserting it “very” correctly.
For these we would need to visually inspect the DC Pins.
User error
This one feels a bit strange but we cannot rule this out.
What is your opinion?
My suggestion would be:
Test PP measurements.
If nothing is found, maybe there is something wrong inside the cable and not afterwards.
Test the PP measurements again but now twisting the cable a bit to simulate if the issue might come from cable.
Make the visual inspection on the DC contacts and see if anything is welded or damaged.
Is this site very far away from your home? If yes, then let me know so that I can recommend spare parts.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

Hello Francisco our savior!
As you probably guessed I was not very satisfied with first responses from the support so I’m very glad you took a closer look!
After the first responses I also plotted all the charging sessions in AWS from this chargers and saw that there were quite many successful charging sessions from the DC4. Basically the same amount than in all the others so this has not been so urgent case (Among all the v5.0.19 hassle). But yes there is still quite a few errors and we should plan a site visit to check it out at some point.
And your there seems to make sense if we have similar issue than in the previous charger in the pictures.
